note: Files: rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (D); day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (E). t1_right/t2_right are stored as ints 0/1, so 'true' is read as == 1 and 'false' as == 0 (bool also accepted); null or missing: not a gap problem. Statistic = budget count / gap count, with R1 = t1_cap_hit is True. n = gap problems; bootstrap over gap problems. kB/kR use the first attempt-0 row per (problem_index, sample), samples 0-3, and count cap-hit rows as not right. These do not affect R1. alt_measured: gap taken as cell == 'rl_only' (the gap text names that cell). It differs only if cell and the right flags disagree. The theory statement says the base capped 'without a loop', but the rule does not test for a loop, and per_problem.json has no loop field, so the script does not test for one.

Files and gap as k1. R2 = not budget, and failure_type lower-cased contains 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected' or 'changed'. Null or non-string failure_type is not taken. The match is a raw substring test, so a label like 'unchanged...' or 'reformatted' would also match. failure_type is one reader's hand label, set only on rl_only rows. I did not look at the label vocabulary, so I don't know if the substrings hit the labels the theory has in mind ('right answer in a rejected or garbled final line', 'reached gold then changed it'). If the labels use underscores (e.g. 'final_line'), 'final line' will not match. That would lower the share; this is the main risk for this number. alt_measured: gap = cell == 'rl_only'.

Files and gap as k1. R3 = not R1, not R2, and kB >= 1. kB counts D rows with attempt == 0, sample 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample) in file order (dedupe after the attempt/sample filter), score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not True. The recipe says cap-hit rows count as not right. D has 1 attempt-0 cap-hit row stored with score_v3 == 1, and E has 3. alt_measured: kB/kR count score_v3 == 1 even on cap-hit rows. Restart rows (attempt 1, 2) are ignored, as the recipe says.

Files and gap as k1. R4 = not taken earlier, kB == 0 and kR >= 2. kR is from E with the same filters as kB: attempt 0, samples 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample), score_v3 == 1, cap-hit rows not right, missing samples not right. alt_measured: cap-hit rows with stored score_v3 == 1 count as right in kB/kR. That can move a problem between capability, reliability and unassigned.

Files and gap as k1. Unassigned = gap problems no rule R1-R4 takes: not capped, no label match, kB == 0 and kR <= 1. refuted_by is coded as measured > 0.06 only. alt_measured: cap-hit rows with stored score_v3 == 1 count as right in kB/kR.

Files: per_problem.json and day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Budget part as k6. Counted if any first-row-per-(problem_index, sample) row with attempt == 0 and sample 0-3 has cap_hit True. Note: the stored T1 sample is not one of these D samples (T1 comes from the S3 r4 run with a different seed), so the samples are independent, as the recipe intends. alt_measured: any row of the problem in D, restarts (attempts 1-2) included, with cap_hit True. A restart only exists after an attempt-0 cap hit, so alt should equal main unless the data break that rule. refuted_by: measured < 0.55 only.

Files: per_problem.json, day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, and the random-cell answers.jsonl as in k6. Reliability part = gap, t1_cap_hit not True, failure_type matches none of the substrings (null counts as none), kB >= 1. So the main number counts stored score_v3 == 1 even on cap-hit rows (literal reading). alt_measured: kB counts cap-hit rows as not right, matching the account's gap definition and k3.
